newsitem.title: GERMANY: German employers stay upbeat on economic outlook.
newsitem.headline: German employers stay upbeat on economic outlook.

text.p: Germany's employers federation said on Wednesday it was sticking to its economic growth prediction of 2.5 percent this year, despite a move by one top research institute to revise down its projection.
Reinhard Goehner, head of the BDA employer group, said on Wednesday it would be possible to achieve the growth figure thanks to rising exports driven by a strong global economy.
He told Saarland Radio the current cold snap would only cause a temporary setback in economic activity.
Goehner's comments came a day after the DIW institute -- one of six whose forecasts are factored into the government budget -- cut its 1997 growth outlook for by half a point to two percent.
But despite his more optimistic view, Goehner said there was no room for complacency because the export-oriented German economy was still losing its global market share.
"The German economy must increase its efficiency," Goehner said, adding that high labour overheads must be reduced to restore economic competitiveness.
Gross domestic product figures for 1996 are due out on Thursday, and economists expect growth to turn out at around 1.5 percent.
